known_facts_book1: Alice's own pet cat, left behind at home — 'Dinah was the cat.'
Never appears in Wonderland; she exists only in Alice's talk and in one dream during the fall.
Alice worries during the fall that nobody will remember Dinah's saucer of milk at tea-time.
Alice wonders 'Do cats eat bats? Do bats eat cats?' while thinking of her.
Alice praises her to the Mouse as good at catching mice and birds, which is what causes the offence.
Talking about Dinah scatters the party on the bank — an old Magpie and a Canary find excuses to go home.
Alice tells the Cheshire Cat and others how well Dinah catches mice.

known_relations_book1.Alice: Her mistress; Dinah is the home Alice keeps returning to in her thoughts.
known_relations_book1.the Mouse: Never meets her; Alice's praise of Dinah is what offends and frightens the Mouse.

known_facts_book1: A Lizard, and one of the White Rabbit's servants.
Is volunteered by the others to go down the chimney of the Rabbit's house while Alice fills it.
Is kicked back up the chimney by Alice's foot; his own account is 'something comes at me like a Jack-in-the-box, and up I goes like a sky-rocket!'
Is afterwards held up outside by two guinea-pigs, being given something out of a bottle.
Serves as a juror at the Knave's trial, and his squeaking slate-pencil is one of the sounds Alice remembers at the end.
Is put back into the jury-box head downwards by Alice after she knocks it over, and waves his tail about helplessly.
Writes on his slate with one finger after Alice takes his pencil, then, when the Queen throws an inkstand at him, writes with the ink trickling down his face.

known_relations_book1.White Rabbit: One of his servants, sent down his own chimney.
known_relations_book1.Alice: Kicks him up the chimney without ever seeing him, and later replaces him in the jury-box upside down. Never an adversary — the two exchange no words.

not_in_this_book: Bill is an enemy of Alice

known_facts_book1: The White Rabbit's housemaid, named but never seen — she never appears on the page.
The Rabbit mistakes Alice for her and sends her home to fetch a pair of gloves and a fan.
Alice hurries through the Rabbit's house 'in great fear lest she should meet the real Mary Ann'.

known_relations_book1.Alice: Is mistaken for her; they never meet.

known_facts_book1: A girl Alice knows outside Wonderland, mentioned only in Alice's own reasoning about who she might have been changed into.
Alice decides she cannot be Mabel because 'I know all sorts of things, and she, oh! she knows such a very little!'
Alice then gets her lessons wrong and concludes 'I must have been changed for Mabel!'
Dreads having to live in Mabel's poky little house with no toys and ever so many lessons to learn.
Never appears, never speaks, and is never in Wonderland.

known_relations_book1.Alice: An acquaintance from Alice's own world, invoked only as a comparison while Alice doubts her own identity.

attribute_confusion: Mabel has long ringlets (the ringlets belong to Ada, the other girl in the same passage)

known_facts_book1: A girl Alice knows outside Wonderland, named once in the same passage as Mabel.
Alice rules her out with 'I'm sure I'm not Ada, for her hair goes in such long ringlets, and mine doesn't go in ringlets at all.'
Never appears, never speaks, and is never in Wonderland.

known_relations_book1.Alice: An acquaintance from Alice's own world, named once as a comparison.
known_relations_book1.Mabel: The other girl in the same passage; the two are alternatives Alice considers and rejects, and they never meet.
